[AtMemory] Show keyboard accessory on textareas with AtMemory only

Behind `kAutofillAtMemorySupportTextAreaOnAndroid`, focusing a
<textarea> shows the keyboard accessory with only the AtMemory entry
point, like contenteditables:

- `ManualFillingControllerImpl` treats textareas as unstructured fields:
  the accessory is shown when AtMemory is available.
- `BrowserAutofillManager` does not generate Autofill suggestions for
  textareas on Android (outside AtMemory trigger sources), so no chips
  ever reach the accessory bar.

Without the flag, textareas keep the legacy behavior of never showing
the accessory.

The approach used in this CL is based on the work done for
contenteditables: crrev.com/c/8176124, crrev.com/c/8214540.

Remove redundant LayerTreeHostImplTimelinesTest fixture

LayerTreeHostImplTimelinesTest was introduced in crrev.com/337751 to
enable compositor animation timelines. It was also used as custom setup
for a smooth-wheel-scrolling workaround for crbug.com/574283.

crrev.com/c/7559274 removed the fixture's use for custom setup, citing
crbug.com/574283 as fixed, but retained the empty fixture because
renaming its tests triggered Android new-test flakiness checks.

crrev.com/c/7962618 then fixed an Android fixture-setup race by
initializing ScopedFeatureList before the task-graph runner starts its
background thread.

With the setup race addressed and those tests re-enabled, we can now
remove the redundant test fixture.

[SafeBrowsing][iOS] Avoid upsampling roundtrip in image resizing

On iOS, `gfx::ResizedImage()` renders into a CoreGraphics context at
scale 1.0, producing a `UIImage` backed by a `CGImage` of the exact
target pixel dimensions. However, calling `gfx::Image::AsBitmap()`
routes through `ImageSkiaFromUIImage()`, which multiplies DIP
dimensions by `ui::GetScaleForMaxSupportedResourceScaleFactor()` (e.g.
3x) and upsamples the bitmap.

Previously, this caused opposing issues at two call sites:
1. `visual_utils::GetBitmapForVisualFeatures()` pre-divided target
   pixel dimensions by `scale` to counteract the multiply. While the
   pre-divide and `AsBitmap()` upsample canceled out dimensionally, it
   rendered the screenshot at `1/scale` resolution before upsampling,
   blurring details across `kPHashBlockSize` boundaries.
2. `ResizeImageForModel()` in `scorer.cc` passed unscaled target pixel
   dimensions to `gfx::ResizedImage()`. While CoreGraphics rendered at
   the exact model dimensions (1x), `AsBitmap()` treated those pixels
   as DIPs and upsampled the bitmap to 3x (allocating a 9x-area,
   ~10.1 MB intermediate on the UI thread), only for
   `skia::ImageOperations::Resize()` to immediately downsample it back
   to 1x.

Introduce `visual_utils::GetResizedImageAsSkBitmap()` in
`visual_utils_ios.mm` to resize directly to target pixel dimensions via
CoreGraphics and convert the result to an `SkBitmap` using
`skia::CGImageToSkBitmap()`. This bypasses `AsBitmap()` and its
resource scale factor multiplication entirely. Update both call sites
to use this helper.

[Keyboard Shortcut Hints] Fix AppMenu item width and 16dp shortcut gap

crrev.com/c/8490136 and crrev.com/c/8520747 changed the AppMenu item
title TextView layout_width from "wrap_content" to "0dp". Because
AppMenu measures row widths with MeasureSpec.UNSPECIFIED, LinearLayout
measured 0dp titles as 0px, preventing the menu from widening to fit
titles and shortcut hints.

Revert the title layout_width to "wrap_content" (with layout_weight="1")
across all AppMenu item layouts, apply @style/AppMenuItemText (9dp
paddingEnd) to menu_item_start_with_icon.xml for consistency, and set
7dp shortcut paddingStart across all layouts for a 16dp gap.

[AIM] Fix RTL omnibox hint truncation after closing AI mode on NTP

omnibox hint remained scrolled to the wider Fusebox viewport offset and

clearing UrlBar focus so empty text hints realign to the beginning of
the restored viewport width.

Fetch: fix the stale bodyUsed assertion in request-disturbed.any.js

The test case "Input request used for creating new request became
disturbed even if body is not used" asserts that new Request(input, {
body }) marks the input's body as used. The Request constructor has not
done that since whatwg/fetch#675 (2018). It creates a proxy for
inputBody, which is what disturbs it, only when init supplies no body:

    If initBody is null and inputBody is non-null, then:
      If inputBody is unusable, then throw a TypeError.
      Set finalBody to the result of creating a proxy for inputBody.

The assertion matches the steps as whatwg/fetch@55141d7 left them in
2017, which disturbed inputBody whenever it was non-null. `#675` limited
that to the case where inputBody is the body the new request uses, and
its tests in #9931 edited this subtest without updating the assertion.

No engine passes the mentioned subtest [1]. Chromium (since
https://crrev.com/c/8451204), Gecko and WebKit all fail it on this
assertion, with "bodyUsed is true when request is disturbed expected
true got false".

[1] https://wpt.fyi/results/fetch/api/request/request-disturbed.any.html

[Passwords] Log structural form signature in internals page

chrome://password-manager-internals currently logs the primary form
signature and alternative form signature, but omits the structural form
signature (which differs from the alternative form signature on forms
with 2 or fewer fields that have a non-empty URL path, query, or ref).

Add STRING_STRUCTURAL_FORM_SIGNATURE ("Structural signature of form") to
SavePasswordProgressLogger and BrowserSavePasswordProgressLogger so all
three form signatures are visible in password-manager-internals logs.

- Update BiDi WebDriver WPT assertions and setup to match the specs so
  the tests pass in Chrome.
- Previously, these tests failed because they included scrollbars in
  the visual viewport size, expected a pointer move to the current
  position to fire an event, computed the in-view center point from the
  bounding rect instead of the first client rect, installed an
  extension from base64 instead of a path, waited for orientation
  change events in a hidden tab, and expected a shifted keyup key
  after releasing Shift.

[glic] Fix guest screen height being 0 during warmup when initially
hidden

When GlicContentsInitiallyHidden is enabled on Windows,
RenderWidgetHostViewAura::InitAsChild leaves screen_infos_ at 0x0 when a
WebContents is created unattached and hidden, causing the guest's
window.screen.height to be 0 during warmup.

Fix this by pulsing IncrementCapturerCount(stay_hidden=true) in
GlicGuestObserver on the top-level WebContents when it is hidden. This
triggers ShowWithVisibility(kHiddenButPainting) -> UpdateScreenInfo() ->
Hide() while keeping the WebContents hidden.

Also add browser tests verifying screen height and frame rendering
across cold and warm reloads and conversation switches in the floating
window.

IME: Use actual inserted length in ReplaceCompositionAndMoveCaret

Previously, InputMethodController::ReplaceCompositionAndMoveCaret
computed the new caret position using text.length(), assuming the full
committed text was inserted. However, when the committed text is
truncated or rejected (for example, due to maxlength on a <textarea> or
<input>), text.length() exceeds the actual inserted length. In a
<textarea> with a trailing placeholder <br>, moving the caret past the
end of the text caused subsequent IME compositions and commits to leave
uncommitted characters behind.

Compute the actual inserted length from GetSelectionOffsets().End() -
text_start after ReplaceComposition() so the caret is placed relative to
the actual end of the inserted text.

Also update the expectation in
editing/inserting/insert-text-nodes-disconnect-on-textinput-event.html,
where TypingCommand::InsertText aborts after the target node is
disconnected during textInput without inserting 'x'. The caret was moved
forward by one character unexpectedly.

OmniboxPopupFullPresenter::IsBrowserOrPopupActive() because Desktop
Aura could activate the Full WebUI omnibox popup (a sibling child
widget) while the browser's platform window was deactivating, leaving

7518c61f1f5791086c9c03336358e49538ba61c7 [ diff ] 
Clear the cached kiosk launch error between KioskLaunchController tests

KioskAppLaunchError::Get() returns a process-global cached value when
one is set, and Save() sets it. KioskLaunchController::OnLaunchFailed()
only saves an error when Get() reports kNone, so that a later failure
does not overwrite an earlier one.

Across tests that combination misbehaves: the first test to fail a
launch leaves the global set, and every later test in the same process
then takes the "already saved" branch and writes nothing, while its own
fresh local state has no launch_error.
KioskLaunchControllerTest.LoadProfileErrorShouldBeStored therefore
passes alone and fails after
KioskLaunchControllerTest.KioskProfileLoadFailedObserverShouldBeFired.

Clear it in TearDown with RecordMetricAndClear(), which already resets
both the pref and the global. The HistogramTesters in this file are
local to the test bodies, so recording at teardown does not affect them.

[iOS][TTC] Log coalesced transcriptions in TtcConversation

Streaming transcription callbacks arrive as incremental word chunks,
which would flood the session journal if logged individually. Accumulate
input and output transcription chunks per turn and update a single
in-place kConversation journal entry (TtcInputTranscription and
TtcOutputTranscription) via TTCJournal::UpdateEntry, resetting the
per-turn state when generation completes, is interrupted, or the session
restarts.

parent
e4b257356a9f66a37f583d87c5bc97468f36cb76 [ diff ] 
[rust] Remove spaces from `rustc_revision` of custom toolchains.

Before this CL, `rustc_revision` was taken verbatim from the
`rustc_version` GN arg when using a custom Rust toolchain (via
`rust_sysroot_absolute`).  The arg is documented as "the output of
`rustc -V`", which may contain spaces - for example:
`rustc 1.100.0-nightly (1edd55dcf 2026-09-09)`.  Such a value breaks
`--cfg cr_rustc_revision=...` in rustflags: `rustc` fails with
"multiple input filenames provided".

After this CL, the same normalization that is already used for the
Chromium toolchain (which removes spaces, among other things) is also
applied to `rustc_version`.

This CL is not really related to Crubit (the main focus of
https://crbug.com/562039310).  But it is related to using a custom
toolchain, so let's still associate this CL with that bug.

android_deps: Bound HTTP thread pools and set POM fetch timeouts

Replace unbounded Executors.newCachedThreadPool() with a 32-thread pool
for POM parsing and license downloads to avoid bursting hundreds of
concurrent connections and exhausting the 512MB Gradle daemon heap. Set
explicit 15s connect and read timeouts on POM and license URLConnections
so stalled connections retry promptly.

🌺 Revert "Update DevTools forbidden extension origins on search engine change"

This reverts commit 1807760946897de70ac399a9377c713b6b95cef1.
Culprit: 180776094689 - "Update DevTools forbidden extension origins on search engine change" (refs/heads/main@{#1718519}, https://crrev.com/c/8579237)

Reason for revert: consistently fails android-internal-desktop-x64-rel.

Mechanism: This CL added
DevToolsUIBindingsExtensionsTest.UpdatesForbiddenOriginsOnSearchEngineChange,
which sets a non-Google default search provider and asserts that
captured_forbidden_origins contains "https://ntp.example.com"
(devtools_ui_bindings_unittest.cc:1721). On Desktop Android
(is_desktop() == true, where kUseWebUiNtpAndroid is enabled by default),
NewTabURLDetails::ForProfile() in chrome/browser/search/search.cc
returns chrome::kChromeUINativeNewTabURL ("chrome-native://newtab/") for
non-Google search engines unless chrome::android::kUseWebUiNtp3PDSE is
also enabled. As a result, search::GetNewTabPageURL(profile_) does not
return "https://ntp.example.com/newtab", causing the new unit test to
fail deterministically on every run on android-internal-desktop-x64-rel
(builds #31310, #31313, #31316) and android-desktop-17-x64-rel-emu-tests
(CI builds #4921, #4922).

DevToolsUIBindingsExtensionsTest#UpdatesForbiddenOriginsOnSearchEngineChange
has failed in 3/3 recent builds of android-internal-desktop-x64-rel,
every attempt in every one of them. This is not flake: it reproduces on
every run, so it blocks the CQ for every unrelated CL that touches this
suite. The regression appears at refs/heads/main@{#1718519}.

Example failing run:
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chrome/builders/try/android-internal-desktop-x64-rel/31316

To run/deflake this test on CQ before relanding, add the following
footer to your CL description:
  Include-Ci-Only-Tests: chrome.android.desktop:android-desktop-17-x64-rel-emu-tests,chromium.android.desktop:android-desktop-x64-rel-15-tests|unit_tests

Reverting to green the tree first. Please re-land once the failure is
understood and covered; this revert is about restoring CQ throughput,
not about the merit of the change.

Original change's description:
> Update DevTools forbidden extension origins on search engine change
>
> DevToolsUIBindings previously computed the forbidden origins list
> (including the default search engine's New Tab Page origin) only once
> when the frontend loaded. If the user changed the default search engine
> while DevTools was already open, DevToolsAPI.setOriginsForbiddenForExtensions
> was not updated, allowing a DevTools extension to inspect the new
> remote NTP.
>
> Observe TemplateURLService in DevToolsUIBindings and re-send the
> updated forbidden origins list to the local DevTools frontend when the
> default search engine changes.
>

[SyncPreview] Rename GetPreferredAccountForPromo to GetPreferredAccountForSignin and clarify docs

Rename AccountPreviewDataService::GetPreferredAccountForPromo() to
AccountPreviewDataService::GetPreferredAccountForSignin(), dropping
"Promo" from the service interface to keep it generic while
distinguishing it from GetPreferredAccountForSwitching().

Update documentation across AccountPreviewDataService, heuristics,
prefs, switches, and UI utilities to clarify that
GetPreferredAccountForSignin() is used when offering signed-out users to
sign in, while GetPreferredAccountForSwitching() is used when offering
signed-in users to switch accounts.

[Omnibox] Plumb ORP to LocationBarLayout

Supply the shared OmniboxResourceProvider owned by
LocationBarCoordinator to LocationBarLayout (and subclasses) via
initialize(), and use its instance methods to resolve activation chip
colors instead of static calls taking an explicit BrandedColorScheme.
LocationBarMediator updates the ORP color scheme before calling
LocationBarLayout#updateVisualsForState(), so results are unchanged.

[Omnibox] Remove test-only Context-based Action constructor

BaseSuggestionViewProperties.Action had a constructor resolving its
description through the static OmniboxResourceProvider.getString().
Production code always passes a pre-resolved description (typically
from the ORP instance), so the constructor was only used by tests.
Remove it and resolve the string in the test instead.

[Omnibox] Use ORP instance methods in FuseboxViewBinder

Replace static OmniboxResourceProvider calls taking an explicit
BrandedColorScheme and Context with the equivalent instance methods on
the ORP already held by FuseboxViewBinder. The shared ORP is updated
with the current color scheme before Fusebox applies COLOR_SCHEME, and
all affected resources depend only on incognito vs. non-incognito, so
the Fusebox-specific APP_DEFAULT collapse does not change the result.

TSF: Remove kDeduplicateSetInputScope feature flag

kDeduplicateSetInputScope was introduced as a kill switch to deduplicate
SetInputScope calls on the same top-level HWND. The feature has been
enabled by default without issues, so this CL removes the obsolete
feature flag and makes the deduplication behavior permanent.

[IME] Scroll focused editable node into view on keyboard expansion

Secondary keyboard expansions (such as opening Gboard Translate or
re-docking the keyboard from floating mode) shrink the visible viewport
further, which can occlude the focused input field. Previously,
onResizeScrollableViewport cleared mFocusPreOSKViewportRect after the
first resize, preventing subsequent height reductions from re-scrolling
the focused editable node into view.

This change ensures the node remains visible across viewport resizes:
* Retain and update mFocusPreOSKViewportRect to track the latest visible
  display frame rect when the viewport shrinks or grows, cancelling on
  width changes (rotation).
* Trigger scrollFocusedEditableNodeIntoView whenever height decreases
  while width is preserved.
* Record the visible display frame on RESULT_UNCHANGED_SHOWN when empty
  and ensure hideKeyboard and non-editable focus states cancel pending
  scroll requests.
* Guard the new retain/re-scroll behavior behind the default-enabled
  kill switch ScrollFocusedNodeOnOSKViewportReshrink; when disabled the
  legacy single scroll per keyboard show is preserved.

[infra] Let android AVD tests run on x86-64-n4|x86-64

Given our AVD test bots have roughly 50% on n2, and 50% on n4 now,
configure emulator-8-cores mixin to request "cpu: x86-64-n4|x86-64"
so 8-core AVD tests can run on either N4 or N2 instances in the
chromium.tests.avd pool. Configure emulator-4-cores mixin to request
"cpu: x86-64" for consistency since N4 instances only support 8 cores.

Remove redundant "x86-64" mixin from emulator builders so the
emulator mixin's CPU dimension is preserved.

Clean up the migration TODOs and temporary optional_dimensions from
android_browsertests, chrome_public_test_apk, and content_browsertests.

parent

Fix SoftwareImageDecodeCache UAF

SoftwareImageDecodeCache had a bug where if image decode tasks were
stopped and restarted there could be a collision on
ImageDecodeRequestId. If the CompositorFrameSink is lost the
ImageDecodeCache object is recreated and
ImageController::SetImageDecodeCache() runs. That calls
StopWorkerTasks() which cancels pending decode requests but didn't
cancel posted tasks. GenerateTasksForOrphanedRequests() then schedules
new tasks reusing the same ImageDecodeRequestId range. If a posted
ImageDecodeCompleted() from before StopWorkerTasks() runs and the
ImageDecodeRequestId matches one of the new request there is a
collision.

The collision can result in a CacheEntry being deleted while there is
still a pending request for it. Avoid collisions by cancelling all
posted ImageDecocdeComplete() tasks in StopWorkTasks().

024fb0519a1cf178a1c4453aa0f8a518d6284f46 [ diff ] 
gin: Annotate Arguments and Runner::Scope as STACK_ALLOCATED()

Follow-up to https://crrev.com/c/8459447. gin::Arguments wraps a pointer
to V8's on-stack callback info and Runner::Scope holds an Isolate::Scope,
HandleScope and Context::Scope, so both can only live on the stack; say
so with STACK_ALLOCATED(). The only class holding an Arguments* field is
internal::Invoker, which is already CPPGC_STACK_ALLOCATED(). Arguments
also drops its out-of-line defaulted destructor; it is constructed and
destroyed on every bound call.

No behaviour change.

[iOS] Only show active permissions in Page Tools

This updates PageActionMenuMediator's isPermissionRowAvailable: to
return NO when the WebState permission state is
PermissionStateNotAccessible, rather than falling back to checking
whether a site-specific content setting exists in
HostContentSettingsMap.

This ensures camera and microphone rows only appear in Page Tools when
actively in use on the current page.

717fddcab1f62755ccb9e36b0b72a6d6d173ca2c [ diff ] 
Pin the Glic system requirement in GlicTestEnvironmentShared

GetDefaultEnabledGlicTestFeatures() enables
chromeos::features::kFeatureManagementGlic so that Glic counts as
supported on ChromeOS, but GlicGlobalEnabling::IsSystemRequirementMet()
reads that feature into a function-local static. The first call in the
process settles it for every later one, so when an earlier test asks
first the features this harness sets up have no effect.

When that happens GlicKeyedServiceFactory::GetBrowserContextToUse()
finds the profile ineligible and creates no service, and
GlicUnitTestEnvironment::SetupProfile() then crashes dereferencing the
null GlicKeyedService in SetFRECompletion().
GlicMetricsFeaturesEnabledTest.TimeToEnabledFromStartupRecorded hits
this and takes the rest of its batch down with it.

Pin the requirement for the lifetime of the harness so the feature setup
above actually takes effect, and reset it in the destructor.

Note this does not cover GlicEnablingTest or
GlicEnablingProfileEligibilityTest, which build their own
ScopedFeatureList rather than using this harness; those are pinned
separately.

#ai-assisted

Cache Storage: make addAll() duplicate detection order-dependent

Per the Batch Cache Operations algorithm, each operation is checked with
Query Cache against addedItems: the put operations that come *before* it
in the batch. Request Matches Cached Item then uses the VARY header of
the cached (earlier) response. The check is therefore order-dependent.
For two puts to the same URL, A with "Vary: x-a" and B with "Vary: x-b",
[A, B] compares the requests' x-a headers while [B, A] compares their
x-b headers, so one order can reject while the other succeeds.

FindDuplicateOperations() instead called VaryMatches() in both
directions for every pair, so it rejected whenever either order would.
This CL compares each operation only against the earlier puts sharing
its URL, using the earlier put's response. The sort becomes stable so
that entries sharing a URL stay in batch order. Firefox already
implements the spec here.

The WPT that covers this, "Cache.addAll should reject when one entry has
a vary header matching another entry" in cache-add.https.any.js,
expected a rejection in both orders, encoding Chromium's symmetric
check. It passed in every engine only because resources/vary.py was
broken; see the PR#63050 [1] for details.

With vary.py fixed alone (wpt PR 63050), Firefox fails the forward-order
assertion in all four variants, because it follows the spec. This CL
therefore also splits the subtest into one per order, expecting success
for [shape, size] and rejection for [size, shape], and drops the [
Failure Pass ] expectation that absorbed the cookie leak.

Behavior change: some addAll() batches that rejected before now succeed,
namely those whose entries only collide under a later entry's VARY
header. Rejections only become rarer, and the result matches Firefox.

[1] https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/63568

[Code Health] Spanify binary_data_histogram_unittest.cc

BinaryDataHistogramTest.Basic built each suffix view with
UNSAFE_TODO(region.begin() + i) and a separate length. Build both the
prefix and the suffix with ConstBufferView's operator[](BufferRegion)
instead, which takes a bounds-checked base::span::subspan(). This is
the existing sub-view API that other Zucchini code already uses (e.g.
zucchini_gen.cc), so the test stays on ConstBufferView rather than
mixing in base::span.

No behavior change: region[{0, i}] and region[{i, n - i}] view the same
bytes [0, i) and [i, n) of kTestData as before. The loop keeps i <= n,
so the subspan() bounds check always holds.

Strengthen the test by checking that the prefix and suffix split
region at offset i. The existing histogram checks did not notice a
suffix taken at the wrong offset: with the suffix changed to
region[{0, n - i}] as a temporary check, only the new assertions
failed.

Remove the base/compiler_specific.h include, which was only needed for
UNSAFE_TODO.

[chromium-bidi] Fix global network interception for popup requests

- Ensure global network intercepts (`network.addIntercept` with no
  `contexts` specified) intercept the initial navigation request of
  newly opened popups.
- Previously, `CdpTarget` chained `toggleNetworkIfNeeded()` after the
  `Network.enable` response, allowing `Runtime.runIfWaitingForDebugger`
  to unpause the popup before `Fetch.enable` was sent.
- Schedule `toggleNetworkIfNeeded()` synchronously after
  `Network.enable` so `Fetch.enable` is dispatched before unpausing the
  target.

GN sets restat = 1 on turbine.py actions because method-body edits do
not change the output .turbine.jar header jar. When android/turbine

c1ddbf2d8f66ef674316ee0fe0554a83699f7eff [ diff ] 
Use DynamicTo when downcasting clip path operation to reference clip

In PaintClipPathAsMaskImage, the mask image painting loop iterates over
a chain of clip path operations. On each iteration, it converts the clip
path operation to ReferenceClipPathOperation using To<T>.

To<T> asserts that the operand is of type T. If a clip path operation in
the chain is not a ReferenceClipPathOperation (for example, a shape clip
path such as circle() or inset()), To<ReferenceClipPathOperation> fails
the type assertion and causes a crash.

Using DynamicTo<ReferenceClipPathOperation> safely returns nullptr if
the clip path operation is not a ReferenceClipPathOperation, allowing
the loop to break gracefully.

The original fix was generated by the Crash Autofix pipeline for crash
report crash/61c3775508400000. Please see go/crash-autofix for more
details. Tweaked to address merge conflict.

[SafetyFRE] Forward full-screen horizontal swipes to the carousel

The carousel RecyclerView only covers part of the carousel screen, so
swiping horizontally anywhere else, e.g. on the title, the buttons or
the margins, didn't change the page. SafetyPromoCarouselView now
forwards horizontal swipes from anywhere on the screen to the
RecyclerView, so the whole screen acts as the swipe area.

Demo http://shortn/_yufx98Ji5x

How the forwarding works:
- ACTION_DOWN: record the start point and the RecyclerView's bounds,
  and let the children handle the event as usual, so taps keep working.
  If no child consumes it, e.g. on a margin, the view keeps the gesture
  itself.
- First ACTION_MOVE that is a single-pointer horizontal swipe beyond
  the touch slop, started outside the RecyclerView: start forwarding.
  If a child had the gesture, intercept it; the framework sends the
  child ACTION_CANCEL. Send the RecyclerView a synthesized ACTION_DOWN
  at the start point, followed by this ACTION_MOVE.
- Later events of the gesture arrive in onTouchEvent and are forwarded
  to the RecyclerView as well.
- All forwarded events are offset into the RecyclerView's coordinates,
  so it drags, flings and snaps as if the swipe had started on it.
- Only the pointer that went down first is tracked; other pointers are
  ignored until forwarding starts, after which the RecyclerView handles
  them itself.
- Swipes within the touch slop, mostly vertical swipes, multi-pointer
  gestures and swipes that start on the RecyclerView are left
  untouched.

Unit tests dispatch touch events through the view, in portrait and
landscape.

Make checkable menuitems be separate <menuitemcheckbox> and <menuitemradio> elements.

The old approach to checkable menuitems was to have a <fieldset
checkable=single> (radio-like) or <fieldset checkable=multiple>
(checkbox-like) be a grouping container for <menuitem> elements that
would become checkable.

Instead, we've decided to create new elements, <menuitemcheckbox> and
<menuitemradio>.  The grouping of <menuitemradio> elements is by their
nearest ancestor <menulist>, <fieldset>, or <menubar>; there is no
explicit grouping mechanism.

This means the menu elements proposal no longer adds attributes or IDL
properties to the <fieldset> element.  Much of the old <menuitem>
behavior now lives on two common base classes: HTMLMenuItemElementBase
which is common to all three of <menuitem>, <menuitemcheckbox>, and
<menuitemradio>, and HTMLMenuItemCheckableElementBase which is common to
only the latter two (and contains common behavior for checkable menu
items).   Submenu-related behavior all stays on <menuitem>.

This is per the latest discussion in
https://github.com/openui/open-ui/issues/1189

Revert "[Media] Validate data origin before mutating UrlData or redirecting"

This reverts commit f558ade080dc27faf1b08af03c0ab50ad461883e.

Reason for revert: Culprit for test failures across Mac, Linux, and Windows CI builders

Failure Link:
- https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/ci/mac13-arm64-rel-tests/79746
- https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/ci/mac14-arm64-rel-tests/53873
- https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/ci/mac15-arm64-rel-tests/34967
- https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/ci/mac15-x64-rel-tests/22385
- https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/ci/Linux%20Tests/187860
- https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chromium/builders/ci/WebKit%20Win10/184460

Original change's description:
> [Media] Validate data origin before mutating UrlData or redirecting
>
> Previously, ResourceMultiBufferDataProvider::DidReceiveResponse()
> called ValidateDataOrigin() only after mutating metadata (such as
> `set_length()`) on `destination_url_data`, migrating to
> `destination_url_data`, and merging cached blocks via
> UrlData::RedirectTo(). Because the newly created `destination_url_data`
> had no `data_origin_` set yet, a same-origin redirect on a subsequent
> range request could adopt a different data origin when answered by a
> Service Worker, and even without a redirect a rejected cross-origin
> response could overwrite `length_` on the shared `UrlData` in
> `UrlIndex`.
>
> Validate `response_url` against both `old_url_data` and
> `destination_url_data` at the start of `DidReceiveResponse()` before
> mutating metadata on `destination_url_data`, inserting into `UrlIndex`,
> or redirecting, and fail the load immediately if either is incompatible.
> Also update `UrlIndex::TryInsert()` so that it returns `url_data` rather
> than an incompatible or unmerged `iter->value` when
> `!url_data->Valid()` or `MergeFrom()` fails origin validation, and
> `CHECK` that `destination_url_data->ValidateDataOrigin(response_url)`
> holds after both `TryInsert()` and `RedirectTo()`.
>
> Fixed: 572308124, 573262234

[FedCM] Fix TSan race in RejectedAmbientRequestFallsBackToRegularUi

In
FedCmAccountSelectionViewAmbientBubbleTest.RejectedAmbientRequestFallsBackToRegularUi,
mutating the process-wide base::CommandLine via ScopedCommandLine inside
TestBody() races with background ThreadPool tasks spawned during
TestingProfile initialization (such as SharedProtoDatabase::InitDatabase
querying base::SysInfo::IsLowEndDevice() ->
base::CommandLine::ForCurrentProcess()->HasSwitch()).

Instead of using kDenyPermissionPrompts to modify the global process
CommandLine, configure the test WebContents's PermissionRequestManager
via set_web_contents_supports_permission_requests(false) so that
AddRequest() synchronously rejects the ambient login permission request
without touching global state.

[ash] boca: take the HostContentSettingsMap in ContentSettingsHandler

ContentSettingsHandler lives in //ash but held a Profile solely to call
HostContentSettingsMapFactory::GetForProfile() on it, so //ash reached
into //chrome for something //components already owns. It takes the
HostContentSettingsMap directly instead, and no longer names Profile or
the factory at all.

BocaUIConfig resolves it alongside the BocaSessionManager it already
passes, and BocaUI holds it until Create() builds the handler. That
sheds one of the three //chrome allowances in ash/webui/boca_ui, and
moves the factory dependency to the //chrome side where it belongs.

The remaining two, for BocaManagerFactory and Profile in boca_ui.cc,
still carry the pre-existing TODO about this layering violation.

#ai-assisted

[iOS] Log Tips click metrics immediately before removal animation

When a user taps a Tip in the Magic Stack, `-didSelectTip:` previously
waited for the 500ms removal animation to complete before calling
`-openTipDestination:` to log `IOS.TipsMagicStack.Module.TappedType`,
`RecordMagicStackClick`, and `NotifyCardInteracted`. If the removal
animation was interrupted, the click metrics and interaction pref update
were dropped.

Log the Tips click metrics and card interaction immediately upon tap in
`-didSelectTip:` before starting the module removal animation.

[iOS] Avoid double-counting TopImpression for ephemeral Magic Stack cards

When an ephemeral card is displayed at index 0 in the Magic Stack,
`MagicStackCollectionViewController` calls both
`-logTopModuleImpressionForType:` and `-logEphemeralCardVisibility:`.
Previously, both methods emitted `IOS.MagicStack.Module.TopImpression`,
double-counting top impressions for ephemeral modules (and falsely
logging a `TopImpression` when swiping to an ephemeral card at index >
0).

Remove the duplicate `kMagicStackTopModuleImpressionHistogram` logging
from `-logEphemeralCardVisibility:` and mark `_hasSeenEphemeralCard`
when swiping to an ephemeral card in `-logNavigationToPage:`.

Android Build: Preserve filtered_jar during partial javac

When compile_java.py takes the partial javac fast path (compiling only
changed .java files and skipping srcjars), it extracts the previous
jar_path into classes_dir before re-creating both jar_path and
options.filtered_jar (*.compliment.jar).

Also extract options.filtered_jar into classes_dir when present. Without
this, partial javac overwrites chrome_java.compliment.jar (1.48 MB, 53
R$* and GEN_JNI classes used on d8's classpath) with a 22-byte empty
zip. Purely a correctness fix (12.05s vs 12.42s on chrome_java).

[WebAuthn] Add RecoverWithICloudKeychain to EnclaveManagerInterface

Add RecoverWithICloudKeychain() to EnclaveManagerInterface,
EnclaveManager, and MockEnclaveManager on macOS. The action runs in
EnclaveManager's state machine: it downloads the passkeys security
domain registration state, recovers the security domain secret from
local iCloud Keychain recovery keys, and stores the recovered key.

The action reports success through a boolean Callback and records its
detailed outcome in the existing per-action histogram
WebAuthentication.Enclave.ActionOutcome.RecoverWithICloudKeychain. If
EnclaveManager is already ready when the action starts, it stops without
downloading or storing anything.

[crubit] Support `extra_rust_sources` in `rust_api_from_cpp`.

Hand-written Rust code sometimes needs to be part of the generated
bindings crate - for example, to implement a foreign trait (e.g.
`TryFrom<CppType> for std::time::Duration`), which Rust's orphan rule
forbids in other crates.

This CL adds an `extra_rust_sources` attribute to the
`rust_api_from_cpp` GN template (mirroring `srcs` of Crubit's Bazel
rules).  The files are passed to Crubit via `--extra_rs_srcs`, using
paths relative to the generated `.rs` file (so that `rustc` can resolve
the `#[path = ...]` attributes emitted by Crubit).

The new `TestTimeDelta` test covers the new attribute, and
`docs/rust/crubit/rust_api_from_cpp.md` describes it together with the
orphan-rule error that it helps to avoid.

[iOS] Inject ReaderModeScrollAnchorJavaScriptFeature at kDocumentStart

ReaderModeScrollAnchorJavaScriptFeature registers the
readerModeScrollAnchor CrWebApi in gCrWeb, which is called from native
code when Reader Mode is activated. Because gCrWeb is injected at
kDocumentStart and the main WebFrame is registered in WebFramesManager
during webView:didCommitNavigation: (before kDocumentEnd), activating
Reader Mode while a page is still loading could invoke
readerModeScrollAnchor.findScrollAnchor before a kDocumentEnd script had
executed, throwing CrWebError: API readerModeScrollAnchor is not
registered in CrWeb.

Inject reader_mode_scroll_anchor at kDocumentStart so the CrWebApi is
registered as soon as the document context is created.

[Test] Declare search box ViewElement in SettingsStation

PasswordsPreferenceTest's MainSettings tests can flake on phones when
SettingsStation#scrollToPref() scrolls before the search box in the app
bar has been made visible.

While https://crrev.com/c/8564038 ensured the RecyclerView's initial
layout pass is complete before entering SettingsStation, on phones
SettingsSearchCoordinator#initializeMultiColumnSearchUi() sets the
search box visibility in a posted task. When scrollToPref() runs before
that posted task executes, the RecyclerView is 192px taller, so the
target preference is aligned to the bottom of the taller list. Once the
search box becomes visible, the list shrinks from the top and pushes the
preference off the bottom of the screen (13-25% displayed), failing
PreferenceFacility's >= 51% displayed check.

Declare R.id.search_box via declareView / declareNoView in
SettingsStation so that entering SettingsStation waits until the search
box is displayed and laid out (on MainSettings or in two-column mode) or
confirmed hidden (on single-column subpages).

Verified with 25 iterations (--repeat=24 --num-retries=0) on
android-14-x64-rel via UTR: 0/75 failures on the 3 MainSettings tests
(150/150 passing across all 6 active tests in PasswordsPreferenceTest),
compared to 23/75 failures without this change.

[ios][Test] Reduce WebTest and WebIntTest flakiness

PlatformTest pushes its outer autorelease pool before WebTest is
constructed and pops it in ~PlatformTest() after WebTest's
WebTaskEnvironment is destroyed. As a result, Objective-C objects
autoreleased during WebState and BrowserState destruction (such as
CRWWebController, CRWWebUIManager, WKWebView, and WKWebsiteDataStore)
outlived WebThread::UI and WebThread::IO, causing deallocations and
WebKit teardown callbacks to run after the task environment shut down.

This CL drains autoreleased objects before WebTaskEnvironment teardown
by:
- Resets crash_observer_ and browser_state_ inside an @autoreleasepool
  in WebTest::~WebTest() before task_environment_ is destroyed.
- Wraps web_state_.reset() in an @autoreleasepool in
  WebTestWithWebState::DestroyWebState() and ensures it is called in
  ~WebTestWithWebState().
- Stops render process crash observation and resets web_state_ inside
  an @autoreleasepool in WebIntTest::TearDown() before clearing
  WKWebsiteDataStore data.

[iOS] Display snackbar on web extension load error

Display a snackbar when an error occurs while loading the Universal
Opt-Out web extension, allowing the user to navigate directly to the
Universal Opt-Out settings page.

- Add WebExtensionErrorSceneAgent to observe ExtensionService load
  error state and present an error snackbar with a "Manage" action.
- Add kUniversalOptOutErrorToastShown profile pref so the snackbar
  is displayed only once across sessions unless reset.
- Add unit tests for WebExtensionErrorSceneAgent.
- If an error occurs before the UI is ready, show the snackbar even if
  the error is fixed.
- Do not show the snackbar in silent mode.

Screenshot: https://screenshot-v2.corp.google.com/2o1019kls0oi0

2b54579ca219d33c3fa9e29c909ea0dd1dcb9a9c [ diff ] 
[webauthn] Accept COSE keys on unknown curves

PublicKey::FromCOSEKey rejected EC2 and OKP keys on any curve other
than P-256 / Ed25519. Such a key made the whole makeCredential
response fail to parse, so the request failed with NotAllowedError.
This breaks, for example, ES384 credentials on YubiKeys.

Instead, return a PublicKey without DER bytes, matching how unknown
key types and unknown AKP algorithms are handled. A missing or
non-integer curve, or bad data on a supported curve, is still
rejected.

[Autofill] AtMemory: Resume fetching messages when reopening the popup

With `kAutofillAtMemorySearchStatefulness`, a search continues in the
background when the popup is hidden, but the fetching timer is owned by
the popup and destroyed with it. On reopening, the first fetching
message was shown, but it no longer rotated until the response arrived.

This CL restarts the fetching timer in `OnPopupShown()` if the search is
still in progress and no (partial) results were received yet.

To model this case explicitly, this CL adds the
`kPartialResponseReceived` search status. It is set when partial results
of an ongoing search are persisted, and reverted to `kSearching` if all
of them are pruned. `IsSearching()` covers both statuses.

[iOS] Remove ForcePortraitOrientationOnIphone helper

Removes the ForcePortraitOrientationOnIphone() helper and the form
factor check, replacing all callers with direct construction of
ScopedForcePortraitOrientation.

Because Chrome declares multi-scene support and all orientations in
Info.plist, UIKit ignores UIInterfaceOrientationMaskPortrait returned by
-application:supportedInterfaceOrientationsForWindow: on iPad and on the
unfolded inner screen of foldable devices, while still enforcing it on
compact phone screens. Always initializing
ScopedForcePortraitOrientation simplifies callers and ensures portrait
lock is enforced if a foldable device transitions to a compact screen
while a portrait-only surface is presented.

Handle setClipboardText failures in ClipboardAndroid

Update Java's Clipboard.setClipboardText() to return a boolean
indicating whether setting the primary clip succeeded. In native
ClipboardAndroid, if writing to the clipboard fails, clear the cached
clipboard map, mark it as out of date, and clear the last modified time.
This is required to keep Android and Chrome clipboards in sync during
copy failures.

Fix UAF when AppWindow is destroyed during Show()

When `chrome.app.window.create()` is called with a window `id` matching
an existing singleton window, `AppWindowCreateFunction::Run()` calls
`existing_window->Show()`. Showing or hiding the native window via
`GetBaseWindow()->Show()`, `ShowInactive()`, or `Hide()` can
synchronously close the native widget and destroy the `AppWindow`
(`AppWindow::OnNativeClose()` -> `delete this`), leading to a
use-after-free both inside `AppWindow::Show()`/`Hide()` and in
`AppWindowCreateFunction::Run()`.

Guard `AppWindow::Show()` and `AppWindow::Hide()` with a `WeakPtr`
check before accessing member state or notifying `AppWindowRegistry`
after the native `GetBaseWindow()` call, and check `existing_window`
liveness via `GetWeakPtr()` in `AppWindowCreateFunction::Run()`,
returning `kPrematureWindowClose` if the window was destroyed.

Remove GpuPreferences::disable_gpu_program_cache

The GpuPreference used to control if GPU program cache was used and had
a command line flag to set it. The implementation bit rotted after it
was replaced by a real GPU workaround with the same name. The
GpuPreference now only impacts tests that go through
InProcessCommandBuffer and not real program cache creation. The
preference is also no longer set from the corresponding command line.

Remove both the GpuPreference::disable_gpu_program_cache and
--disable-gpu-program-cache. Users can still set the workaround from
command line with --disable_gpu_program_cache=1.

[Ambient] Elide IdP domains at the start

The IdP name of a federated credential is a domain, e.g. "idp.example",
whose end is its most significant part. Previously, a long IdP name was
elided at the end like other text in the bubble, e.g.
"very-long-idp.example" became "very-long-id…".

Now, it is elided at the start instead, e.g. "…long-idp.example", both
in the collapsed bubble and in the expanded list of credentials. The
provider names of other credentials are still elided at the end.

In the expanded list, the IdP name is on the third line (the footer) of
a row that shows both an account name and an email, and on the second
line (the subtitle) otherwise:

  [pic] Carol               <- title
        carol@example.com   <- subtitle
        …long-idp.example   <- footer

  [pic] dave@example.com    <- title
        …long-idp.example   <- subtitle

To elide the correct label, the rows use a HoverButton subclass, since
only subclasses can access HoverButton's labels below the title.

[PartitionAlloc] Fix inspection and plotting tools

Update the C++ inspection binaries and Python analysis scripts in
//tools/memory/partition_allocator to work with current PartitionAlloc
internals.

The main changes are:
- Support external metadata (MOVE_METADATA_OUT_OF_GIGACAGE)
- Remove the requirement of same-address mapping. The ASLR range is
  quite small (256GiB) on ARM64 macOS, and the tool already has 32GiB
  worth of PA itself, so mapping failures are frequent. Since the tool
  was last used, fewer things in PartitionAlloc rely on absolute
  pointers, making the change quite small.
- Small build improvements for macOS, and drive-by small python
  modernizations.

process_launcher: Handle missing connection exception

This patch guards ChildServiceConnectionImpl.rebindService and
BindingRequestQueue.flush against IllegalArgumentException thrown by
ActiveServices.updateServiceBindingsSingleLocked when a child service
connection has already been removed in AMS (for example, due to a child
process crash before onServiceDisconnected is processed on the launcher
thread):

1. In ChildServiceConnectionImpl.rebindService, check isBound() and
   catch IllegalArgumentException, matching updateGroupImportance().
2. In BindingRequestQueue.flush, wrap Context.updateServiceBindings in
   try/catch/finally so mBindingRequestQueue.clear() and
   TraceEvent.end() always run. When IllegalArgumentException is thrown
   (which aborts the batch loop in AMS), fall back to applying each
   queued item individually via rebindService/unbindService so valid
   updates in the same batch are not lost.

      "*ScopedServiceBindingBatchImplTest*:*ChildProcessConnectionTest*"

[Composebox] Route remaining searchbox metrics through common helpers

Add recordCount() to cr_components/composebox/common.ts and use the
existing recordUserAction()/recordBoolean()/recordEnumerationValue()
helpers in ntp_searchbox.ts and current_tab_chip.ts instead of calling
chrome.histograms directly.

The helpers fall back to chrome.metricsPrivate when chrome.histograms
is unavailable, which is the case in extension pages. This is a step
towards hosting these components outside of WebUI.

The one behavior change is in voice search: it used to bail out when
chrome.metricsPrivate was missing, which is the case on
chrome://omnibox-everywhere.top-chrome since that host isn't in the
metricsPrivate allowlist. VoiceSearch.Action.{OmniboxPageContext} and
VoiceSearch.Errors.{OmniboxPageContext}, as well as the
VoiceSearch.Action and VoiceSearch.Errors aggregates, are now recorded
there too.

[Code Health] Spanify ui/base/x/x11_util.cc

Replace the three UNSAFE_TODO buffer accesses in ui/base/x/x11_util.cc
with safe C++ and base::span constructs:
- In SetUseOSWindowFrame(), copy MotifWmHints into the property vector
  via base::as_writable_byte_span() and base::byte_span_from_ref().
- In SetWindowClassHint(), pass the WM_CLASS data to SetArrayProperty()
  directly via base::byte_span_with_nul_from_cstring_view() instead of
  copying it into a vector using pointer arithmetic past str.size(). The
  trailing NUL is required and a plain cstring_view to span conversion
  would omit it.
- In GetNativeWindowIcon(), slice the icon pixel data with
  base::span::subspan() and copy into the SkBitmap via
  gfx::SkPixmapToWritableSpan().

Add x11_util_unittest.cc to cover the exact WM_CLASS property bytes,
including the trailing NUL, and the icon pixel copy.

[AtMemory] Cancel pending queries on filter change

Previously, pending queries were only canceled when the filter became
empty. This updates AtMemoryManager to cancel ongoing queries whenever
the filter changes, preventing stale query results from returning.

[Account Settings] Clear settings before notifying on sync disable

AccountSettingSyncBridge::ApplyDisableSyncChanges() notified observers
of each setting update before clearing `settings_`. Observers reading
the setting from within OnDataUpdated() thus saw the stale value. As a
result, PersonalContextEligibilityService did not detect that context
sources became disabled and did not fire OnContextSourceDisabled(),
leaving e.g. the AtMemory cache populated.

Clear `settings_` before notifying, consistent with
ApplyIncrementalSyncChanges().

[APC] Omit unknown ARIA roles from page content

A missing, empty, or invalid role attribute currently produces an
aria_role value of kUnknown in actionable page content. Leave this field
unset when no recognized role is available.

Resolve the role once with DetermineRawAriaRole and reuse it for
landmarks, dialogs, ARIA form controls, and interaction information.
Remove an unused parameter and a redundant check, and add tests for
unknown roles and fallback tokens. Keep role=none and role=presentation
in the output as kNone.

[MiraclePtr] Enforce raw_ptr in templated containers in ios/chrome/browser/{browsing_data,fullscreen}

This change replaces instances of raw C-style pointers (`T*`) with
`raw_ptr<T>` for elements stored inside templated containers (such as
`std::vector` and `std::array`). This aligns with the broader MiraclePtr
safety initiative to protect against use-after-free vulnerabilities.

This advances MiraclePtr's expansion to containers and preempts an
upcoming clang-plugin update that will strictly ban these un-rewritten
instances.

Bug: b:501142609
Doc: go/miracleptr-in-containers
DanglingUntriaged-notes: Dangling pointer found by checks after the
rewriting to `raw_ptr` was performed.

parent
4836fcab016c1f14f3b9f68573f9c48756e32de0 [ diff ] 
[Media] Validate data origin before mutating UrlData or redirecting

Previously, ResourceMultiBufferDataProvider::DidReceiveResponse()
called ValidateDataOrigin() only after mutating metadata (such as
`set_length()`) on `destination_url_data`, migrating to
`destination_url_data`, and merging cached blocks via
UrlData::RedirectTo(). Because the newly created `destination_url_data`
had no `data_origin_` set yet, a same-origin redirect on a subsequent
range request could adopt a different data origin when answered by a
Service Worker, and even without a redirect a rejected cross-origin
response could overwrite `length_` on the shared `UrlData` in
`UrlIndex`.

Validate `response_url` against both `old_url_data` and
`destination_url_data` at the start of `DidReceiveResponse()` before
mutating metadata on `destination_url_data`, inserting into `UrlIndex`,
or redirecting, and fail the load immediately if either is incompatible.
Also update `UrlIndex::TryInsert()` so that it returns `url_data` rather
than an incompatible or unmerged `iter->value` when
`!url_data->Valid()` or `MergeFrom()` fails origin validation, and
`CHECK` that `destination_url_data->ValidateDataOrigin(response_url)`
holds after both `TryInsert()` and `RedirectTo()`.

[iOS] Add NTPThemeActionableTipConfig and wire in TipsMagicStackMediator

Standard Magic Stack tips use `TipsModuleConfig` (a subclass of
`IconDetailViewConfig`), which is coupled to the informational
icon/title/description layout (`IconDetailView`). Unlike informational
tips, the actionable NTP Theme tip allows users to customize their NTP
background directly from the card via 5 circular theme/photo swatches, a
custom header without a separator, and a "See more" button.

Because it requires a distinct view and container configuration, this CL
introduces `NTPThemeActionableTipConfig` as a direct subclass of
`MagicStackModule`. `TipsMagicStackMediator` retains `_config` so
existing callers (such as `ContentSuggestionsCoordinator` impression and
interaction logging) can continue reading
`_tipsMediator.config.identifier`, while exposing `activeConfig`
(`MagicStackModule*`) so the Magic Stack can display `_actionableConfig`
when the actionable `kNTPTheme` tip is active.

More details can be found under actionable tips section in the WIP DD
go/magic-stack-v2

Changes:
- Create `NTPThemeActionableTipConfig` subclassing `MagicStackModule`.
- Update `TipsMagicStackMediator` to instantiate
  `NTPThemeActionableTipConfig` when reconfigured with
  `TipIdentifier::kNTPTheme` and
  `IsMagicStackTipsV2IosActionableEnabled()` is true.
- Expose `activeConfig` on `TipsMagicStackMediator` to return
  `actionableConfig` when present, falling back to `config`.

[iOS Testing] Add hooks to control tracing from EG Tests

Add methods to Chromium's EarlGrey interface:
* stopStartupTracing: Stops the trace initiated by the
  --trace-startup command line flag, flushes it to disk, and
  returns the trace file path.
* startManualTracing: Starts an interactive trace session.
* stopManualTracing: Stops the trace session previously started by
  `startManualTracing`, flushes it to disk, and returns the trace
  file path.
* isTraceFileReadyAtPath: Checks whether a trace file exists and has
  a non-zero size inside the application container.
* traceDataForPath: Reads the trace file inside the application
  sandbox and transfers the content as an NSData over EarlGrey EDO
  (IPC) to the test process, enabling consistent trace analysis on
  both simulators and physical devices.
* removeTraceFileAtPath: To clean-up traces written by a test.

Includes TracingTestCase in tracing_egtest.mm to validate both startup
and manual trace control and verify slice generation via Perfetto SQL.

These interface methods were implemented to help with automating
performance testing and performance investigations.

[views] Avoid text shaping in Label default tooltip checks

views::Label::ShouldShowDefaultTooltip() is 0.83% of Browser main
thread jank [1]. It runs when a label's text or bounds change, and
shapes the whole text with HarfBuzz to check whether it fits.

Fix: behind the LabelDefaultTooltipFastPath feature, avoid text shaping
when the result of ShouldShowDefaultTooltip() can be determined without
it: there is no tooltip if the text is empty or obscured, and there is
one if the content width is zero (common, because labels typically get
their text before being laid out). Also skip the redundant
UpdateTooltipText() call at the end of Label::Init().

Some of the removed work is only postponed: labels measured for layout
later reuse the shaped text. But the work is eliminated for labels that
are never measured or whose text changes before layout. In a Linux
browser test exercising UI seen in jank profiles [2], this eliminated
25% of the text runs shaped by HarfBuzz (shaping cache misses) at
startup (window title, initial tab title, hidden bookmark bar buttons),
and 20% when opening another window with a cold cache. Elsewhere, the
work was mostly postponed.

The fast path introduces minor behavior changes in edge cases, which we
think are desirable or harmless. See LabelTooltipTest.*:
TooltipOfMultiLineLabelWithZeroContentWidth,
TooltipHandlerOfLabelWithEmptyText and
TooltipOfZeroWidthTextWithZeroContentWidth.

[1] http://pprof/?id=8f1c2496b26f253176d7e249f70d384f&pivot=views::Label::ShouldShowDefaultTooltip
[2] https://crrev.com/c/8542153

NTP Promos: Fix crashes due to invalid UE contexts

Per a spot-check of NTP promo-related crashes, there is evidence of a
crash in promo code. AI established that it happens when an NTP tab is
dragged from one window to another, the old window is closed, and then a
promo is clicked. The Web UI handler caches the UE context, which will
now be invalid, and hence cannot be used at that time. Rather than
checking validity, it's better to derive the context when needed, to
ensure we get the right context (other Web UI handlers do it this way).

Also:

* Ensure that if we don't have a valid context, we don't invoke any
  promo callbacks.  This ensures individual promos don't have to handle
  this unexpected case themselves.
* Remove some now-needless Create() constructor wrappers, and adjust how
  the unit tests mock the UE context.

[devtools] Migrate service worker web tests to CDP (4/N)

Migrates 3 legacy DevTools web tests 1-to-1 from
http/tests/devtools/service-workers/ to
http/tests/inspector-protocol/service-worker/, and deletes 2 that are
already covered there. The tests only assert on backend behavior; the
DevTools frontend was just the vehicle for sending protocol commands.

Migrated (together with their worker scripts
resources/network-fetch-worker.js and resources/service-worker-debugger.js,
which no other test uses):
- service-worker-network-fetch.js
- service-worker-network-fetch-blocked.js (uses Network.setBlockedURLs
  on the service worker target, as the frontend's request blocking does)
- service-worker-pause.js
The two fetch tests share a small resources/network-fetch-helper.js that
replaces ApplicationTestRunner.makeFetchInServiceWorker. The baselines
are unchanged apart from the new location of the worker script, and the
line numbers in service-worker-pause, because git cl format reformats
the moved service-worker-debugger.js.

Deleted as redundant:
- service-worker-manager.js: checks that a service worker target is
  added on registration and removed on unregistration. This is covered
  by inspector-protocol/service-worker/target-events.js
  (Target.targetCreated/attachedToTarget on registration,
  Target.targetDestroyed on unregister).
- offline.js: checks that toggling offline mode with an active service
  worker does not crash (crbug.com/746220). Covered by
  inspector-protocol/service-worker/offline-service-worker.js, which is
  extended here to also switch offline mode back off and check
  navigator.onLine.

Legacy expectations are removed, not carried over, and no new entries
are added for the migrated tests. This drops the SlowTests entries for
service-worker-pause.js (crbug.com/1043354) and
service-worker-network-fetch-blocked.js (crbug.com/1046784).

parent
a599176bcfa1cd15871122663b34b95734702cda [ diff ] 
android_webview: Make AwPacProcessor.destroy() thread-safe

destroy() can delete the native object while another thread is calling
into it, for example the network callback on the ConnectivityThread.
The pointer checks from crrev.com/c/7736909 don't prevent this, because
destroy() can still run between a check and the JNI call.

Guard all of AwPacProcessor's state with a read/write lock. PAC
evaluations hold the read lock, so they still run concurrently.
destroy() and the methods that update the network hold the write lock.
The lock is fair, so new evaluations can't keep a writer waiting.

So that destroy() doesn't wait for in-flight evaluations to finish, it
first cancels the native jobs under the read lock, which also fails any
later ones. It then deletes the native object on the PAC thread without
waiting for it.

[Dictation] Make multiline dictation over a selection a single undo step

When the first transcript for a richly editable target is multiline,
Target falls back to pasting. Before pasting, it committed empty text to
cancel any existing composition, which split undo into two steps: the
first undo removed the paste, and a second was needed to restore the
original content.

Skip the empty commit when nothing has been composed, so the paste
replaces the selection in a single undoable edit.

[sync] Avoid adding default shelf pinned apps in SyncTest

When SyncTest reuses the primary Ash profile ("test-user") for client 0,
ChromeShelfController is attached to GetProfile(0). Once APP_LIST and
OS_PREFERENCES start syncing, IsSafeToApplyDefaultPinLayout() becomes
true and ChromeShelfPrefs::AddDefaultApps() pre-allocates pin positions
in AppListSyncableService for uninstalled default apps (with empty
item_name), breaking SingleClientAppListSyncTest expectations.

Change ChromeShelfPrefs::SetShouldAddDefaultAppsForTest() to accept
std::optional<bool> so tests can override ShouldAddDefaultApps() to
either true or false, and set it to false in SyncTest::PostCreateThreads().

[devtools] Migrate signed exchange web tests to CDP (3/N)

Migrates 5 legacy DevTools web tests 1-to-1 from
http/tests/devtools/sxg/ to http/tests/inspector-protocol/sxg/:
- sxg-navigation.js
- sxg-navigation-fail.js
- sxg-navigation-redirect.js
- sxg-cert-not-found.js
- sxg-transfer-size.js

These tests only assert on backend behavior (the browser-side
Network.signedExchangeReceived event, the network events of the outer,
certificate and inner requests, and the Log entries for signed exchange
errors). The DevTools frontend was only used to collect them.

The tests now use a small shared resources/sxg-helper.js that collects
the raw Network and Log events. It prints the requests in the same
format as NetworkTestRunner.dumpNetworkRequestsWithSignedExchangeInfo,
so the network part of the baselines is unchanged. Differences:
- Log entries are printed as "Log entry (<level>): <text>" instead of
  the frontend console format "about:blank:1 <text>".
- sxg-transfer-size now logs its checks instead of using silent
  asserts. Like the frontend, it attributes the Network.loadingFinished
  encodedDataLength of the inner response (reported by the OOPIF
  target) to the signed exchange.

No other test sends or checks Network.signedExchangeReceived
(content/ and chrome/ browser tests only exercise the loading path,
and there are no existing inspector-protocol sxg tests), so nothing is
deleted as redundant.

sxg-disable-cache.js, sxg-prefetch.js and sxg-prefetch-fail.js stay
for a later batch.

Legacy TestExpectations entries are removed, not carried over, and no
new entries are added for the migrated tests. This drops the
[ Mac14 ] and [ Mac14-arm64 ] Failure entries for sxg-cert-not-found.

[MiraclePtr] Enforce raw_ptr in templated containers in ios/chrome/browser/overlays

This change replaces instances of raw C-style pointers (`T*`) with
`raw_ptr<T>` for elements stored inside templated containers (such as
`std::vector` and `std::array`). This aligns with the broader MiraclePtr
safety initiative to protect against use-after-free vulnerabilities.

This advances MiraclePtr's expansion to containers and preempts an
upcoming clang-plugin update that will strictly ban these un-rewritten
instances.
